nodes.title: SG-11 Drive character animations and scene transition from game actions
nodes.body:
Context: BootScene already plays the character idle loop on create, plays interact then idle when a character sprite is clicked, and plays the authored fade once in create(). ReactToPhaserEvents already declares playAnimation and transitionTo, but nothing emits or handles them, so game actions such as object actions and dialogue choices never reach the Phaser scene. Desired behavior: performing a game action in the app screen makes the boy play the interact animation and then return to idle, and a scene change replays the scene transition, all through the Phaser scene. Expected result: unit tests confirm interact and transition are triggered from game actions. Why: the app screen should visibly react to gameplay.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given the BootScene is created, when a playAnimation event targets a character, then that character sprite plays the named animation and returns to idle
- Given the app is playing, when an object action is performed, then a playAnimation interact event is emitted for the boy
- Given the BootScene is created, when a transitionTo event is received, then the scene transition is played through the Phaser scene
- Given a game action that moves the scene, when it is performed, then a transitionTo event is emitted


## Scope
- In scope: BootScene subscription to playAnimation and transitionTo
- In scope: App emitting those events from game actions
- In scope: Unit tests for both directions
- Out of scope: New assets or new scenes
- Out of scope: Backend or API changes
- Out of scope: Visual redesign
- Preserve: Existing click-to-interact behavior on character sprites
- Preserve: Idle animation on create and the transition on create
- Preserve: Typed event bus contracts for existing events


## Technical constraints
- Phaser 3.90 with Phaser mocked in unit tests
- Use the existing reactToPhaser bus and event types in game/frontend/src/phaser/events.ts
- No duplicated game state ownership


## Definition of done
- Requirements implemented with unit tests passing
- Events are unsubscribed on scene shutdown


## Non-functional requirements
- No Phaser listener leaks after scene shutdown


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · BootScene plays character animations and the transition on React events
nodes.body:
Context: events.ts declares playAnimation {target,name} and transitionTo {sceneId} but BootScene never subscribes. Desired behavior: BootScene subscribes in create(), plays the requested character animation then returns to idle, replays the scene fade for transitionTo, and unsubscribes on SHUTDOWN. Expected result: Phaser reacts to React commands. Why: lets game actions animate the scene.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a character with an interact animation, when playAnimation {target:'boy',name:'interact'} is emitted, then the boy sprite plays the interact animation key and replays idle on ANIMATION_COMPLETE
- Given a transitionTo event, when it is emitted, then the camera fadeIn is called with the authored transition duration
- Given the scene has shut down, when playAnimation or transitionTo is emitted, then nothing is played


## Scope
- In scope: BootScene.create subscriptions
- In scope: Per-character play method keyed by id
- In scope: Shutdown unsubscribe
- Out of scope: Walk animation movement
- Out of scope: Loading new scenes
- Preserve: createCharacter click behavior
- Preserve: playSceneTransition call in create


## Technical constraints
- Use reactToPhaser from ./events
- Reuse ensureAnim and resolveCharacterAnimation


## Definition of done
- BootScene handles both events and releases them on shutdown


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · App emits interact animation and transition events from game actions
nodes.body:
Context: App passes game.act to ActionMenu and game.choose to StoryPanel without telling Phaser. Desired behavior: after an object action App emits playAnimation {target:'boy',name:'interact'}, and when the action changes the active scene id it emits transitionTo. Expected result: unit tests show the events are emitted from game actions. Why: the screen reacts to gameplay.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given the playing view, when an ActionMenu action is chosen, then reactToPhaser emits playAnimation with target boy and name interact
- Given a game action that changes the scene id, when it completes, then reactToPhaser emits transitionTo with the new sceneId
- Given an action that leaves the scene id unchanged, when it completes, then no transitionTo is emitted


## Scope
- In scope: App wrapper around game.act
- In scope: Scene id change detection from game state
- Out of scope: Adding new scenes or content
- Out of scope: StoryPanel layout changes
- Preserve: game.act state updates
- Preserve: objectClick and menuClose bridges


## Technical constraints
- Use the existing reactToPhaser bus
- Do not mock the store in unit tests of state change


## Definition of done
- App emits both events from the action handler


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: Act: Subscribe BootScene to playAnimation and transitionTo
nodes.body:
Add subscriptions in BootScene.create that look up the character sprite by id and play its animation then idle, and replay the transition through the effect context. Release them in the SHUTDOWN handler.

## Acceptance criteria
- playAnimation plays the named animation on the matching character and returns to idle
- transitionTo calls playSceneTransition with the scene and effect context
- Shutdown removes both subscriptions


## Scope
- In scope: game/frontend/src/phaser/BootScene.ts
- Out of scope: Tests
- Out of scope: App changes
- Preserve: Existing click handler behavior


## Technical constraints
- Phaser 3.90 APIs only
- Code path: `game/frontend/src/phaser/BootScene.ts`


## Definition of done
- BootScene handles both events and cleans up


## Clarifying questions
- None
nodes.summary: Add reactToPhaser handlers in BootScene.create and release them on shutdown
nodes.description: Add subscriptions in BootScene.create that look up the character sprite by id and play its animation then idle, and replay the transition through the effect context. Release them in the SHUTDOWN handler.
acceptance_criteria: playAnimation plays the named animation on the matching character and returns to idle
transitionTo calls playSceneTransition with the scene and effect context
Shutdown removes both subscriptions
definition_of_done: BootScene handles both events and cleans up

steps.action: Extract the click body that plays interactKey then idleKey into a method stored per character id: add a private Map<string, (name: string) => void> field characterPlayers, and register in createCharacter a function that plays interactKey for name 'interact' (when interactKey exists and differs from idleKey) then plays idleKey on ANIMATION_COMPLETE, and plays idleKey otherwise; call the same function from the POINTER_DOWN handler after emitting characterClick.
steps.code: this.characterPlayers.set(spec.id, (name) => { if (!idleKey) return; if (name !== 'interact' || !interactKey || interactKey === idleKey) return; sprite.play(interactKey); sprite.once(Phaser.Animations.Events.ANIMATION_COMPLETE, () => sprite.play(idleKey)); });
steps.expected: Clicking a character behaves as before and the player is reachable by id

steps.action: Import reactToPhaser from './events'. After playSceneTransition(ctx, scene) add two subscriptions stored in a private offReact array: reactToPhaser.on('playAnimation', ({target, name}) => this.characterPlayers.get(target)?.(name)) and reactToPhaser.on('transitionTo', () => playSceneTransition(ctx, scene)). Reset this.characterPlayers = new Map() before creating characters.
steps.code: this.offReact = [reactToPhaser.on('playAnimation', ({ target, name }) => this.characterPlayers.get(target)?.(name)), reactToPhaser.on('transitionTo', () => playSceneTransition(ctx, scene))];
steps.expected: Events from React play the animation and the transition

steps.action: Inside the SHUTDOWN handler call each function in this.offReact, set this.offReact = [], and call this.characterPlayers.clear().

nodes.title: Act: Emit playAnimation and transitionTo from App game actions
nodes.body:
App passes a wrapped action handler to ActionMenu that performs game.act then emits playAnimation for the boy and emits transitionTo when the scene id changed.

## Acceptance criteria
- Choosing an action emits playAnimation boy interact
- A changed scene id emits transitionTo


## Scope
- In scope: game/frontend/src/App.tsx
- Out of scope: Tests
- Out of scope: BootScene changes
- Preserve: game.act and game.choose behavior


## Technical constraints
- Read the scene id from the game store state after the action
- Code path: `game/frontend/src/App.tsx`


## Definition of done
- App emits both events


## Clarifying questions
- None
nodes.summary: Wrap game.act in App to emit reactToPhaser events
nodes.description: App passes a wrapped action handler to ActionMenu that performs game.act then emits playAnimation for the boy and emits transitionTo when the scene id changed.
acceptance_criteria: Choosing an action emits playAnimation boy interact
A changed scene id emits transitionTo
technical_constraints: Read the scene id from the game store state after the action

steps.action: Change the events import to also import reactToPhaser: import { phaserToReact, reactToPhaser } from './phaser/events'.

Add handleAction(objectId, actionId): record the previous scene id from game.state.sceneId, call game.act(objectId, actionId), emit reactToPhaser 'playAnimation' {target:'boy', name:'interact'}; read the new scene id from useGameStore.getState().state?.sceneId and, when it differs from the previous one, emit 'transitionTo' {sceneId}. Import useGameStore from './store/gameStore'. Pass onAction={handleAction} to ActionMenu in place of game.act.
steps.code: const handleAction = (objectId: string, actionId: string) => { const prev = game.state.sceneId; game.act(objectId, actionId); reactToPhaser.emit('playAnimation', { target: 'boy', name: 'interact' }); const next = useGameStore.getState().state?.sceneId; if (next && next !== prev) reactToPhaser.emit('transitionTo', { sceneId: next }); };
steps.expected: ActionMenu actions emit the Phaser commands
